Dust billows as Mydei slams a Kremnoan alpha to the ground. He grips the alpha by the arm, looming above him. His muscles flex and sweat drips down his temple as he pushes his weight forward into the alpha’s back. After a few heavy breaths and a trembling, meager contest to dislodge from the vice grip, he calls for release. Mydei obliges.

Other Kremnoans are gathered around the open air gymnasium, some standing off to the side while others sit on benches, watching their crown prince instruct on the finer details of hand to hand combat with a live demonstration. The alpha joins the cluster of defeated warriors who jumped at the chance to spar with their prince, nodding his head in approval over his prowess. Great strength, after all, is a valuable feature to possess.

Mydei turns to the eager ones who wait, and calls out, “Who wants to try me next?”

An omega warrior approaches. His shoulders are drawn taut, his jaw clenched in agitation, and his fists ready to spar. Mydei remembers him. He was the one who caused a scene a day ago about his status as an omega— one he had to intervene in before it devolved into a bloody fight. As anticipated, his people struggle to acclimate with their long standing enemy: the city-state of Okhema.

Instead of invading the Holy City, he forces them to live with begrudging passivity. And, as proud warriors, they take issue with his ambitions. Mumblings sprout of how different his rule would be if he were an alpha. He is told he would have been more fierce in his disposition, and taken his rightful role as a conqueror. The thought leaves a bitter taste.

When he wishes for his people to acclimate and not throw their lives away in conflict, they question his decisions. To turn away from tradition and play house with Okhema—the word blasphemy clings to the tips of their tongues. Grips between their teeth. Yet they follow his decree, for none can best him in a duel to change his thinking.

The omega warrior lowers himself into a fighting stance, and Mydei honors him with the same respect.

In the Holy City, omegas are ones who provide for the home, who help run families. Not join militaries and become soldiers. Mydei once scoffed and called them “pets” when he first learned of this, and Aglaea—a beta like himself—scolded him.

“They are not pets,” she said. “There is a different ideology housed within the walls of Okhema. They are not people who have been instructed in the art of warfare, nor have they been taught the values of ‘valorous death before glorious return.’ Take a careful look with your very own eyes, and see if they are as you say. I am sure someone as keen as yourself will understand.”

Pain brings comfort. It has been his constant companion for a long, long time. The first of his memory is choking on water clogging his lungs. Many more remembrances tear through his flesh, spilling golden blood from every slash, pierce, and hammer upon his immortal body. Every wound taught him lessons words can never breach; and so, too, can he understand others through conflict.

Like how much this omega detests his station as a soldier questioned. He allows for the bout between him and this warrior to extend; allows him to air his grievances over Okheman’s insulting his pride and having no opportunity to defend his honor with a bloody duel.

At first he would have agreed with his sentiments at the notion of omegas being tutted as too delicate for war, but with a different scrutiny, he became aware of something new. For the first time, he witnessed a life beyond never ending strife, and of how much more it can be. How much fondness and warmth came from children running to their parents. How households created a space for safety and love.

The first time he observed and witnessed this life without prejudice clouding his vision, his heart ached with want. Though, his people do not see what he sees. They find no pleasures of simple living where one can return home to a loving family. They wish to brandish steel and surrender their souls to Strife. To die with a wound through their chests as their greatest aspirations. His soul withers at the thought of such aimless ambitions.

Punches land on his torso. His arms are gripped with frightening strength. Even if he allows this omega some grace, he can never let him have the upper hand, for he is the crown prince. He stands alone above his people with no equal.

Mydei pins the omega warrior underneath him, knee to his back, and claims his victory. With every breath he takes, all he smells is dirt and sweat. No pheromones flow through the air, but those around him scrunch up their nose from an invisible thread.

“Who’s next?” He turns to the crowd, and an alpha stomps her way forward. This one, he remembers, is the omega’s companion who bore witness to her friend’s plights of yesterday.

“Your Highness,” she says, pounds a fist upon her chest in salute. “I cannot allow these Okheman swine to continue insulting our honor. They laugh at our omegas, claim them to be weak.” She spits on the ground. “They should be taught lessons on who is truly weak. A single Kremnoan omega can kill ten of their alphas. Let us show them what they deserve.”

A dull ache develops in the front of his head.

There are no more battles to draw spear and bow for. Marching across mountains, through marshes and valleys—it no longer offers a distraction. The mad King Eurypon has been slain by the Kremnoan Detachment. Castrum Kremnos is now a bygone city, no longer illustrious with power.

With no more conflicts to fight as an army, he has to deal with conflicts of society—these strange secondary dynamics he has no interest in.

Before, he was able to wave his hand away at these issues. This strange world of ‘scenting’ and ‘marking’ and how it perverses them. How it bothers them to such intrinsic levels it transforms them into different people. A peaceful living gives way to these different troubles. Those he has no interest in learning.

In an ideal world, everyone would be a beta like him. Reasonable and never once arguing over who smells like what or whom.

“If you defeat me in battle, I shall permit such things,” he says.

Pain may have been a terrible teacher, but it taught him how to win. How to fight against every opponent and come out on top. The alpha soldier takes her steps and stands in front of him, visage twitching with stifled fury.

“You may have the first move,” he offers.

With no hesitation, she surges forth. Her form is perfect from years upon years of training. Nurtured in the art of war before she turned the tender age of five. And he aches with this knowledge, this brutal way of living should be no more.

She manages to trap him in a headlock, her muscles straining in the squeeze, but he twists around and gains the upper hand with ease, then suplexes her onto the ground. The dust picks up once more. He holds her trapped until she has to give in.

“Your strength has no equal, Your Highness,” she says with heavy breaths, subdued by his power.

Though her words are false. There is one person who he claims as his equal: the alpha Deliverer, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae. But the pride of his people disallows them to acknowledge an alpha outside of their tribe.

They met outside the Holy City, and he tested him in a duel. After the grueling death match lasting ten days and nights with no victor, he thought he found his equal, but his people scoffed. He asked his respected alpha teacher Krateros why that was, and he answered thus:

“The crown prince of Kremnos has no equal. Especially not when it comes to an alpha whose very nature demands submission. It is an insult to you to call him as such. It is ignoble to bear his scent and fraternize with the witch’s loyal servant. You must keep your distance, Mydeimos. No good can come from his company.”

The undertow of his words carried him far beneath the surface, and he took them to heart at first; he ignored every belligerent attempt at conversation, every invitation to spar declined. Yet, the sunbeams penetrated the dark river, and he found himself floating towards them, hand outstretched.

And as his fingers grazed the light he questioned: who else would he find worthy to watch his back? Who else in this world could be his equal?

“You are strong,” he honors her, and stands. “I hear and understand your concerns. The plight of our people is not lost upon me. I bear your words, and all the omegas who suffer underneath the Okheman prejudices. But we cannot allow ourselves to be so easily swayed by provoking words. As Kremnoans, we must understand they wish to use underhanded tactics.”

“Pah, as all Okhemans want to do.” She lifts herself off the ground and straightens out, no longer rubbing the bruise forming on her arm. “Those hyenas hide with the knowledge of us following the laws of this land, and think themselves strong. Be it an equal battlefield, they would already be swimming in the Sea of Souls.”

At least his people are subdued from the most recent incident. Mydei stifles the groan bubbling beneath the surface. This will undoubtedly be repeated within a few days. This same bickering over and over again drains him— pulls at every corner of his patience.

With his people temporarily calmed, he turns to patrolling the city in the second quint of Action Hour. Once he steps outside the boundaries of the Kremnoans, eyes of strangers glue to his back. Distrustful Okhemans watch his every step, though quite a few have eased to his presence.

It’s grueling work to gain the trust of the masses. Thankless in many ways. But he needs to set an example for everyone. To show that he and his people are not war mongering, selfish brutes.

From a distance, he spots two children watching their friend try to climb a tree. At the top branches, a ball wedges between the foliage. The child scampers up until his grip weakens and he lands on his butt with a thud. His friends gather around him.

Mydei steps forward. “What are you three doing?”

“We’re trying to get our ball back!” The one on the ground says, glaring up at the treetop. The other two gawk in surprise.

“It’s the crown prince!”

“His Highness is here to help us!”

“Crown prince?” he mutters underneath his breath. “Are you three Kremnoan?”

“Yeah!” The one on the ground stands. His knees are scuffed.

“Why haven’t you three gotten an adult to help out?” he asks.

“Because our parents are busy, and all these Okhemans are a bunch of wusses!”

“Right…” he chuckles softly. “I’ll help you out, but you have to promise me the next time this happens you won’t try climbing up this tree on your own, and get an adult to help.”

The three of them nod eagerly. With that, he jumps to action, nimbly climbing up the branches. The children clamor in excitement. It barely takes him a minute until he’s at the very top. A familiar, cheerful voice calls out as his fingers brush the ball.

“Why, is that Mydei?” Phainon gazes upwards, a grin plastered on his face. “You really are a cat, climbing up so high in the trees! Are you going to take a nap there as well?”

“His Highness is helping us get our ball back!” the girl with bright red hair says.

“Oh, is he now?” Phainon says, and Mydei ignores the amused lilt in his tone. “How valiant is the prince, coming in your time of need.”

“He’s so awesome!” the boy beside him exclaims, his knees and elbows scuffed with his attempts to climb. “It took him only a minute to climb up to the top.”

“Yeah, because he saw you falling and then yelled at you for not getting an adult,” the blonde girl says with her hands on her hips.

“Hey! I almost got up there!”

“If it took the prince a minute to get up there then it would take me thirty seconds,” Phainon joins in, placing a proud hand upon his chest. The children all glimmer with excitement.

Mydei doesn’t understand the Deliverer’s strange fascination with boasting about his skills in comparison to his. And he doesn’t understand why it gets underneath his skin. His ears twitch with every proclamation of how better he is, and his blood boils.

Without an ounce of hesitation, Mydei hurls the ball down. It impacts Phainon’s skull with a loud smack, knocking him off balance. The boy chases the bouncing ball and scoops it up.

“If you are so eager to prove yourself, then fight me right here, right now,” Mydei says, slinging himself off the branch and landing beside him.

“Did you really have to do that?” Phainon rubs his head as he rights himself. “Talk about pettiness. That’s really unbecoming of you.”

“Hmph, whatever you say, Deliverer. Or perhaps you’ve grown so soft you can’t handle a simple throw.” He crosses his arms before turning his attention to the children. “Go. Enjoy your games. And get an adult if you lose it again.”

Phainon is about to open his mouth to continue on with his bantering, but his pupils constrict into pinpricks, and a low, dreadful growl rumbles through his chest. His lips curl back into a sneer as his nostrils flare in his inhalations. Mydei raises a curious brow over the sudden change in his disposition.

The children go from excitement to squeaking in terror. “Thank you, Your Highness!”

They run off, and Phainon’s gaze never tears from him. He takes a step forward, flashing his fangs in contempt. Another growl reverberates as leans in close, and inhales at his neck. The hair on his nape raises.

“What is with you?” Mydei asks in discomfort, but remains rooted in his spot. To back away would be a sign submission.

“Huh?” Clarity returns to Phainon with a blink. He takes a step back and the darkness eclipsing his visage vanishes. “I—” His eyes dart back and forth as nervousness overtakes him. “Did I do something?”

“You were growling at me like an animal. Did I hurt your feelings?” he mocks, relief easing through him.

“N-No!” He frantically waves his hands. “It’s just—Uh…”

“Spit it out. I don’t have all day.”

He swallows. “Did… Did you have relations with someone?”

Mydei stares at him.

“Like… You know…” He gestures with his hands.

“No, I don’t know. I have relations with my people. I speak with Aglaea and Castorice on the daily. What are you talking about this time?” His brow ticks in annoyance.

“Did you sleep with someone?!” Phainon blurts out.

The exclamation takes him by surprise.

“What are you talking about? Of course I haven’t.” Never once has he expressed interest in such a thing. Why in the gods names would Phainon think such a thing?

“Are you sure?” He squints in disbelief. “You’re covered in the smell of an alpha.”

Of course, these stupid dynamics continue to butt their heads in all aspects of his life. “Do such things matter? I was training my tribe in hand to hand combat.”

“Of course they matter!” he flusters. “It’s distracting. We should head to the baths right this second.”

“Or what? Your eyes will go cross from jealousy?”

“I’m-! I’m not jealous! Don’t say such ridiculous things, Mydeimos.”

“Quit acting like an alpha, we’re still on duty,” he scolds. “It would be unbecoming as warriors of Okhema to run off to leisures when we need to maintain peace.”

“A quick, ten minute dip in the baths is not an invitation to spend the rest of Action Hour soaking. Besides, you’re all dirty from climbing up that tree,” Phainon clings to a minuscule reason, gesturing wildly with his index finger. “We can’t have the crown prince of Kremnos walk around with leaves in his hair.”

“There are no leaves in my hair,” he says, but rakes a gauntleted hand through his hair and dusts his robes. “If you really find problems with a scent on me, we can simply patrol two different sections of the city.”

He takes a step in the other direction.

“No!” Phainon shouts a bit too loudly, and intercepts his stride. “I mean— why not go to your house and take a wet rag to rub yourself free of it? It doesn’t take much to get rid of a scent. I promise.”

The headache from earlier returns. He really doesn’t want to be dealing with this.

“Why does it matter so much?” he dryly asks.

“Because-!” Phainon puffs up his cheeks like a child. “You should be more aware of your position. Kremnoans might not care as much, but citizens of Okhema—”

“Who are you implying isn’t a citizen?” Mydei glowers. He might let the Deliverer fumble his words, but he will not stand for the exclusion of his people.

Phainon bites his tongue. “That’s—You know that’s not what I meant.” He sighs, shoulders wilting. “Just—can you please be a bit more considerate to your new home?”

And for how much Phainon annoys him on the daily, he hates seeing that crestfallen look upon his visage. It tugs nonsensically at his heart strings, softening him into something he is not and never was.

A deep sigh rattles through him. His belligerence eats at his patience, and he deliberates over what might relieve him from this stress. Then, with careful words he mutters, “Would you be more at peace if you scented me?”

Phainon blinks, the stupid expression on his face almost makes Mydei chortle. “What?”

“I don’t wish to return all the way to my home while on duty, and waste my time wiping myself with a cloth,” he says, though that unfamiliar sensation coursing through his immortal body hopes Phainon takes the invitation.

“That is—I—Huh—?” he stutters as if the words are lodged in his throat.

“What?” Mydei resists the urge to rub his temple. “Perhaps it would be a good thing for all citizens to see me bearing the Deliverer’s scent,” he reasons, though his attempt to convince sounds as if he speaks to himself as well. “A way to symbolize the unification of my people and a willingness to integrate.”

Phainon’s throat bobs in a heavy swallow. His golden pupils dilating the blue expanse of his iris. “If—If you’re sure.”

“I wouldn’t speak it if I weren’t,” he huffs, embarrassment tinges his cheeks with Phainon’s insecure delaying.

He grabs him by the elbow, and drags him behind a building, bringing him underneath an arbor trellis; the flowers bloom above them, bright and vivid purples, and the light from the Dawn Device gives them no privacy.

“You’re sure,” Phainon presses again, searching his features as if he proclaimed in jest.

“Don’t make me repeat the same words over and over,” he says. “I already agreed to humor you and your ridiculous alpha ways. If you continue hesitating I will resume patrolling. We’ve wasted enough—”

No more seconds are spared. Phainon grabs his shoulders, invades his personal space, and lowers his cheek to press against his neck. One back and forth rub on the right. Then on the left. The edges of his hair tickle his nose, and he discreetly inhales.

All he can smell is the tinge of shampoo and the flowers hanging overhead.

“There,” Phainon says, cheeks colored red like a delicious pomegranate. His fingers dig into his shoulders. He breathes in through his nose, then frowns. “Wait—No. Just a little more.”

This time, he’s careful. The rubbing of skin against skin is more measured. The softness of his cheek presses against his defunct scent glands on his neck. And, somehow, even he feels the intimacy of this. His heart picks up pace of its own volition, discomforting him. He rubs a thumb across his chest, trying to quell the sudden blooming of warmth expanding throughout his body.

It’s an odd sensation—one he’s never felt and leaves him befuddled. It’s not the searing fire scorching his veins in the heat of combat. It’s not the rush of returning to life after trudging against the current of the Sea of Souls. It’s something calmer… something…

Phainon’s nose buries into the crook of his neck, pressing against his glands, and inhales. A pleasant hum reverberates through his throat. The tip of his nose rubs up against his neck, and the delicate skin of his lips brush alongside, finding comfort in something he cannot. Those hands drift down his shoulders, fingertips brushing his arms.

And Mydei wonders what must have taken his attention; he’s been told in the past betas have their own miniscule, muted scents, but it can’t be this enticing. If he were an omega, these actions would be understandable. After all, their saccharine scents are meant to entice alphas. Lure them in. Hold them close. Make a family together. And—

He shoves him off.

“Haikas,” he mutters as he looks off to the side. “I think you’ve imparted your scent well enough.”

Phainon regards him with a look he can’t quite name—it softens the edges of his eyes, and his lips curl up into a gentle thing. Whatever it is, he refuses to meet it; refuses to admit the increased fluttering of his heart. His hands clench in the crossing of his arms.

“I think I can go for another pass,” he says. Mydei huffs and walks off. Phainon follows, trailing after him like a pleased puppy.

As they patrol through the streets the people regard him with a more friendly attitude seeing him walk side by side with Phainon. The man has a natural charisma which draws others to him, and he can’t deny he fell for it as well. By this point he understands it as the way of life: the Deliverer is warm and generous—the type to draw anyone in.

A few omegas grab Phainon’s attention as they pass by their stall of an assortment of foods, and he heads over to make sure everything is alright.

Mydei crosses his arms as he waits off to the side, tapping restlessly against his bicep.

Their giggling annoys him. Their excited cooing irritates him. Their fluttering eyelashes makes him want to cave their faces in. And these thoughts frustrate him. What’s wrong with him? These feelings only sprout whenever omegas take up too much of Phainon’s attention. Whenever he gives them that damned smile of his.

Which is ridiculous. Nothing they have done warrants such violence from him.

He glances over, and spots Phainon’s red face as he denies something with a shaking of his head.

He doesn’t mean to eavesdrop, but he hears the omega ask, “Did you— you know,” and then does an odd gesture of snapping their teeth at him which causes Phainon to jolt in shock and shake his head more fiercely. They laugh more.

“No!” Phainon’s panicked voice rings loudly. “Nothing of that nature! You are all mistaken we’re…” His remaining words are left unheard as he returns to a normal volume.

Must be some strange alpha and omega conversation. A flash of fire burns through him, and he clenches his jaw, the muscle along his neck pulsing in the strain, and he fears he may crack his teeth if this continues.

“Deliverer, you can keep dallying if you so desire, but I have better things to do,” he calls out, and turns on his heel. He’s been ready to leave for the past five minutes.

He hears Phainon say, “Mydei-! Wait!”

A few strides down the street, and hurried steps chase after him. “You are so impatient.”

An infuriating sense of relief washes over him, and he quarrels with how much his mood improves.

“Here.” Phainon holds out an apple in front of his face, cheeks still flushed. “A gift. They insisted I give this to you.”

“Why?” He eyes it wearily.

“Who knows,” Phainon scoffs, and turns away. “I don’t think you deserve it after ditching me.”

“Quit being dramatic.” He grabs it and takes a bite with a loud crunch.

Phainon’s gaze flickers between him and the road ahead before asking with an uncharacteristic shyness, “Is it good?”

“Mm.” He takes another large bite. Another loud crunch and explosion of sweetness upon his tongue. His sour mood from moments ago completely dissipates.

Phainon seems too pleased with himself. He decides to ignore it. But, it’s hard to ignore how closely he walks alongside him. How their arms brush. How he can spot the dark bags underneath his eyes with clarity. How Phainon’s voice dips low and he has to lean in to hear. Has he always been this touchy? Maybe the invisible scent he bears emboldens his actions.

And a shiver runs up his spine when Phainon presses a palm against his back as they navigate through a crowded street; right on top of his weak spot.

He roughly shoves him off. “Quit treating me like an omega.”

Phainon startles, then laughs. “I’m not treating you in such a way. I didn’t want us getting separated. Would you prefer for us to hold hands instead?” He waves it around in a mocking gesture.

Mydei narrows his eyes at his pertness.

“Mhm, that’s what I thought.” He steps back close and their shoulders brush. “I’ll stay my hand if it so pleases you.”

He responds with a grunt, and focuses on moving through the street, trying to ignore the soft touch and how it soothes. Ignoring how he didn’t mind the hand on his back and would appreciate its return.

After a few quints they eat dinner together. Such a thing is normal for them, and the owner greets them like regulars. They find a table in the back, and order a variety of foods ranging from meats to fruits.

“You’re not sleeping well,” Mydei states after their waiter walks off.

“Hm?” Phainon tilts his head, pretending to be confused.

“Don’t be obtuse, Deliverer. I see it written all over you.”

“If I didn’t know any better, I’d wager you are worried for me,” he banters. “And don’t accuse me of such things when I can see the same on you.”

His words are founded in truth; countless nights he has spent restlessly staring at the ceiling of his home. How can he sleep with the never ending pressures and responsibilities thrust upon him? When his desires run against a thousand years of tradition.

“Besides, we both know our limits. How many days and nights did we fight without a moment of reprieve? A night or two of insomnia is hardly a thing worth considering.” Phainon brushes off the concern with practiced ease.

Mydei knows he speaks in falsehoods. Such weariness painting his visage does not come from a couple of restless nights. It comes from weeks. Months. Maybe even years for someone like him.

“Hmph. A dull, uncared for blade is the weakest weapon of all,” he states.

“Are you suggesting you’ll oil me up and massage my tense back?” he asks with a glint in his eye.

“No.” He pinches the bridge of his nose, fighting how his stomach flips at the thought of running his hands down his back. Feeling the firm muscle underneath his bare hands. “Quit twisting my words.”

“I think we have bigger things to worry about.” Phainon’s gaze flickers behind him as he stifles his giggles, and the waiter comes back with a multitude of plates filled to the brim.

Mydei gives polite words of gratitude to their waiter as he juggles a row of plates on each arm, and miraculously places each and every single one of them down.

“Alright Mydeimos, let us see who can eat their meal the fastest, shall we?” Phainon throws him a look which never fails to get underneath his skin. The sort of sly smile uncharacteristic of the man known as the savior.

It taunts him fiercely, influencing him to eschew his regal demeanor.

He begins to devour and stuff his face.

“Hey-! I didn’t do a countdown, you’re cheating!” Phainon quickly follows suit.

It’s a playfulness he has never been afforded in this life of his until now. Something so light-hearted and insignificant, yet thrilling. The head start secures him an easy victory. And with victory, he can gloat over how much better he is while Phainon grumbles and whines over his secret duplicitous nature.

Deeper into Parting Hour, they pass by a few alpha and omega Kremnoans. They eye the Deliverer wearily. He grins in return, flashing his teeth, and takes a casual step closer to his side. His people bristle, but they hold their tongues in front of their prince. Their exchanges are curt, and they glare all the while.

At least the betas hold normal conversations, and it eases him from the tense atmosphere. Whatever silent communication happens is lost upon their innocent bubble of naivety. With nothing out of the ordinary needing to be addressed, they continue on their way.

But his back prickles with their stern looks.

“What did you do?” he asks in a grumble.

“Me?” Phainon innocently points at himself.

“Did you do something I’m unaware of to anger my people?”

“No, certainly not,” he says. “You see, Mydei, if you ever actually do pay attention to what I say about alphas you’d know. There’s this thing called —”

Phainon rambles, and he tunes him out. He tends to go on these long tirades when it comes to the politics of secondary genders. He already has enough on his mind. Paying attention to this dialogue between alphas and omegas, one he has no knowledge of, never incurred any interest.

The final quint of Parting Hour approaches, and they pass through Marmoreal Palace. The baths are speckled with a few people going about their evenings, soaking into the comfortable waters, feasting on delicate fruits.

“ —Are you listening to anything I’m saying?” Phainon nudges him as the elevator brings them up to the Hero’s Baths, voice tinged with annoyance.

“No.”

He humphs and crosses his arms. “Fine, continue to remain clueless. It’s a perfect look for you after all. The Clueless Prince of Kremnos, only caring when it comes to himself.”

Mydei rolls his eyes. The two disrobe themselves, sparing no customary courtesy of covering themselves with bath house towels or attire. After all, they have this place to themselves. They hardly need to cover their nudity when they are the sole visitors.

“I really don’t understand why you refuse to learn,” Phainon continues. “You know how important it is to everyone. Even you have a scent you know, as muted as it may be.”

His people have told him about it before. They say he smells like bread. Bread of all things. The first time he heard it he scoffed and found it unpleasant. Who wants to go around smelling like a pastry?

“And what does my scent say that I could not, Deliverer?” he bites back. “Such things are ridiculous. I don’t need to rely on these nonsensical ways to detect emotions when I can understand them as clear as day.”

They slink into the hot bath, shoulder to shoulder, and Phainon lets out a pleased groan as his muscles relax.

“Well.” Phainon’s eyes glint. “Dare I say it?”

“What?”

“Oh, maybe I shouldn’t,” he teases, slinging an arm across the ledge behind him, hovering near his shoulders but not quite touching. “I might insult the delicate heart of the crown prince. Then his people will really have my head.”

“My people have plenty of other reasons to be cross with you,” he says.

“Well—” the word clings to the tip of his tongue in his enunciation. Then, he bites his lip in hesitation. “I could tell you liked it when I scented you.”

Mydei snorts. “I know you are bold at times, but not to the point of absurdity.”

“You might say one thing, but I did detect the sweetening of your scent.” He taps the tip of his nose. “This of mine works. Unlike yours. You should trust me more on these things.”

“You are playing mind games with yourself. I know alphas and omegas can’t detect such things within betas. We are stable, unlike you lot.” He leans away and turns his nose up at the audacity. “I don’t need you to be a hound.”

Phainon barks out a laugh. “I have to disagree! After all, I was as close to the source as I could be.” He shifts forward, invading his space with a grin. “You liked it. It’s alright to admit it, Mydei. I understand. I am quite amazing after all.”

“I am told the Deliverer is a humble man,” Mydei says as he shoves his face away. “Why don’t you practice some of that humbleness they speak of?”

Phainon grips his wrist and twists his arm. “I am certainly humble. I listen to the wishes of others, unlike a certain someone who refuses to listen to his dear companions' attempts to assist him.”

“Listening to a hyena speak is akin to surrender.” He grapples Phainon’s arm with his free hand, forcing himself out of the twisting of his arm. Their muscles strain against one another in the beginning of a small bout of wrestling. “And Kremnoans never surrender.”

“Maybe you should try it! It will be a good look for you.” Phainon pushes him back.

They devolve into a slippery match in the baths. The water sloshes around between them as they punch and push. Nothing with any amount of real force—a playful, familiar banter. In the back of his mind, Mydei craves this type of normalcy. Craves the simplicity.

A space where he holds no worry about ruling and governing; a space where he can enjoy himself without the scrutiny and expectations of his people. Where he can enjoy the simple squabble of nonsensical drivel from Phainon.

And, in the back of his mind, he wonders what Phainon must smell like right now. His smile is grand, his laughter echoes through the baths in his exultation. Is it sweet? He’s heard people describe it—something akin to fresh linens toasting underneath the sun sprinkled with a pleasant citrus. Is it ripening right now? Is it becoming more with every contact of wet skin against skin?

He wants it to be.

Every grip and touch upon his muscles sears with a pleasant heat— especially when the Deliverer presses his hands against his chest. His nipples harden with accidental brushing. His heart rate spikes when he’s grabbed by the waist and shoved. And every time he grips him in return, the shape of Phainon clings to his skin. It’s… nice. It’s nice to be able to grin without worry.

Phainon does that gesture he witnessed earlier—snapping his teeth at him in a playful bite. It’s cute in a strange way. If there is a meaning to it, it is lost upon him, but he mimics it in return. In that moment, Phainon flusters, his grip slips, and Mydei uses it against him to gain the upper hand.

Unbeknownst to Mydei, the air laces with sickeningly ripe and potent pheromones; sharp enough to make any alpha scrunch up their face and omega to choke on the headiness. No one will know.

“Okay, okay!” Phainon clamors when he’s pinned against the edge of the bath, the ledge digging into his sternum. “You don’t smell like fresh honeycakes covered in jam when you’re happy!”

Mydei hovers behind him, pinning his arm against his back as he leans in closer to murmur in his ear, “Good. I’m glad you finally see reason, Deliverer.”

A shiver travels up Phainon, and he opens his mouth to respond—

A clicking of heels interrupts their contest, and both of them swivel their heads to face the intruder.

“Boys,” Aglaea’s stern voice carries through the hall. She’s dressed in a light robe, ready to bathe in the waters, and carries two extra sets in her arms. “What did I say about bathing in the nude?”

Mydei sinks down so his ass is no longer exposed in the air, then lets go of Phainon.

“That it’s only allowed during Curtain-Fall Hour?” Phainon offers.

“No,” she corrects with exasperation. “That you two are to be respectful and mindful to everyone who wants to partake, and dress yourselves.”

Mydei reclines against the ledge, face flushing in embarrassment as he crosses his arms.

“But no one reserved it. I checked the list before we entered.” Of course Phainon continues to try to find an out. “I wouldn’t be so careless to discard my attire if I knew someone wished to bathe at the same time.”

“And why does the reservation list exist in the first place?” She tosses the extra sets of robes and it lands on their heads. Mydei promptly starts dressing himself.

“That was one time Aglaea! We’ve been good since,” he continues to protest.

“One time is all it takes for rules to be set into place. Hurry up and dress yourself, Cas wishes to join.”

“She does?” Phainon tilts his head, his voice wavering with sudden nervousness.

“Yes.” Aglaea gestures with her hand for him to hurry.

He wraps it around himself, fumbling with the edges of the fabric. For once, the Deliverer has no witty retort. Aglaea calls out to Castorice, and her delicate footfalls thump against the marbled flooring. Maybe his silence comes from the fact Castorice is an omega. Okheman alphas always tend to act odd around them, especially with any amount of revealing skin.

Mydei quite likes the fact Aglaea is a beta like him. It supplies him with an amount of confidence in himself as a leader. She has governed for a millennia, and proved to be effective. If she can, so will he.

And when Castorice steps inside, dipping her feet into the baths a safe distance away, her eyes flicker between Phainon and Mydei.

“It’s good to see you joining us, Miss Castorice,” Phainon says with a forced smile, drawing her attention.

“Likewise, Lord Phainon,” she says and settles in. “It has been a long day.”

And so a light discussion between all parties begins to brew. For Mydei, he always finds it odd how rarely they speak of grueling conquests or the desire for glory of days long past. Instead, they fancy topics about delicious foods, Castorice’s hobby for crochet and writing, and gossip over mundane happenings.

Phainon for once is awkwardly quiet. His attention focuses on his hands clasped on his lap, oddly tense for the banter moments prior. His face is flush from what Mydei assumes to be caused by the heat of the bath.

The Deliverer’s silence bothers him. Normally, by this point, his ears would begin to ring from how loud his voice carries in his excited yapping. Instead, he stares at the water in front of him still as a statue.

Mydei elbows Phainon underneath the water, and he glances over. “Yes?”

“What is wrong with you?”

“Nothing is wrong,” he assures. “I think I’m starting to get a bit too tired to keep up with the conversation.”

“Then retire to your chambers,” Mydei says, though he can sense his lies. The way he holds himself is too stiff, as if he has something else on his mind. But he decides against pressuring him if he’s too uncomfortable to speak on it.

“I think I will.” He stands and bids farewells to the entire group with a smile plastered on his face. Mydei’s gaze trails his departure until he turns the corner and is no more.

Castorice turns her attention to him. “Did something happen between the two of you?”

“Nothing unusual. Why?”

She hums and taps her chin in thought. After a brief moment, she decides to say, “Lord Phainon’s scent is quite strong today.”

“Is it not strong at all times?” he responds dryly.

“Yes, but today is different.” She offers a gentle smile. “It’s nothing to worry about. He must have enjoyed himself today.”

Her refusal to elaborate leaves him frustrated, but he refuses to ask why out of stubbornness. He’s not that interested in whatever the Deliverer fancies from day to day. And he tends to act odd at any given moment. Though, he’s not stupid. The only difference today was the fact he allowed himself to be scented.

Did it seriously make him so happy even Castorice could tell from this distance?

“If you say it is nothing to worry over, then I’ll pay it little mind,” he says, and she covers a giggle behind her hand.

“Maybe you should pay it more mind. After all, Lord Phainon is often hard on himself. Bringing a small piece of joy makes the world a little bit brighter in these trying times. Wouldn’t you agree?”

“I…” Whatever he wanted to say dies before it can be uttered. The scurrying of the High Priestess Tribbie interrupts their conversation, and she cannonballs straight into the baths. The tide from their impact splashes against all of them.

She giggles and proclaims, “We got all of you!”

Mydei wipes the water off his face, watching as Tribbie makes her way to his side and sits on the ledge next to him, splashing her feet in the hot water. He remains quiet as the others speak in earnest about their days, about the rumors spreading on their teleslates, about how Aglaea wishes to maim Caenis.

“Are you alright, De?” Tribbie asks him suddenly while the other two continue chattering.

“Hm?”

“You seem like you have a lot on your mind.”

“Ah…” He closes his eyes and takes a breath. “It is nothing worth worrying over. Thank you for your concern.”

“If you ever need someone to talk to, know that we are always happy to help!” she beams.

“I appreciate the sentiment, Lady Tribbie.”

When he leaves for home, Castorice’s words continue to echo through his head. They reverberate as he lays on the kline. They scream as he stares at the ceiling when sleep refuses him. He raises a hand forward, tracing the tendons connecting to his knuckles before bringing it down to rub his eyes.

Maybe he can let him do it again…

No, he shouldn’t. These strange alpha omega politics should be avoided at all costs. He already has enough on his plate to worry about—putting his people first, making sure they can integrate into the Holy City. Soften the prejudices against them. Defend against the black tide. Hunt down Nikador and slay him. Those are his first and foremost priorities, not making the Deliverer wag his tail over scenting.

So, with his resolve settled, he continues about his duties as normal. He trains with his people first as is customary for him. A spark of relief flashes through them when he stands beside them, and his scent proves to be untainted.

Before training commences in full, Krateros pulls him aside, a frown marring his features.

“What is it?” Mydei asks.

“Mydeimos,” he begins, his grave tone indicating his disapproval. “I’ve heard rumors and whispers of what occurred yesterday.”

“And what has happened which gives you pause to pull me aside for a private conversation.” He bites back the groan threatening to spill through. He knows exactly what he intends to bring up.

“Do not let that low-born soldier scent you again. It is unbecoming as the crown prince of Kremnos.”

Of course it is. If he didn’t respect his teacher, he would have rolled his eyes and dismissed his impudence.

“How is it so unbecoming? We should show more of our willingness to work together with the Holy City. We can’t let ourselves hold onto this belief of segregation,” he tries to reason.

“Your words would hold merit if he were an omega,” Krateros rebukes. “But he is not. I understand your unwillingness to subjugate yourself to these dynamics, but an alpha scenting is not so easily dismissed. It is a sign of power to the alpha and submission to the recipient. Our people cannot see you in such a light when they already protest your unwillingness to plunder Okhema in rightful glory.”

“Having the Deliverer scent me is hardly a sign of difference in respect and strength. We have already proved ourselves on equal footing with our long conflict which ended with no clear victor.” He grinds his teeth and holds his tongue on speaking about conquests and razing Okhema—their eternal enemy—to the ground, and reaping their wealth.

“If only it were so simple.” He shakes his head. “Our people revere you as their prince, and wish for you to ascend to the throne as king. A king has no equal and stands proud above all. You cannot bow your head and let the authority of an alpha wash over you.”

“I am not,” he says. Images of Phainon’s soft smile after scenting him flicker. Was that really the face of someone imposing a claim? “The Deliverer will never hold such ground over me, this I can promise.”

“Good.” Krateros relaxes as his worries ease. “I am glad you understand.”

But he does not understand. It’s just a smell, one he can’t detect. It lingers in the empty space he can’t breach. It creates unrest within his people— unrest within himself, casting disruptive thoughts, penetrating his structured semblance of peace.

Alpha Kremnoans crowd around him more that day, corralling him into the center of their pile during their training and skirmishes. They request more close quarter combat, brushing upon his skin with an air of pretendful ignorance.

He figures what they attempt to do after an hour: they wish to impart their collective scents upon his skin by proxy. Remind Okhema of his Kremnoan nature and status. Repel any form of idea of integration with their ways of life.

And it irritates him. He pretends their plans go unnoticed for their sake, but a calm fury roils within. This separation his people continue to impose. The desire to return home, to follow the ideals which have driven them to untimely deaths over and over again. Why do they cling to it so readily when Amphoreus trembles upon the brink of annihilation?

What sort of pride can they find when they throw away the last moments of their lives to an endless battle covered in blood instead of enjoying their moments with their kin? Where can pride linger when they perish against an enemy with no beating heart, with a will only knowing destruction, and leave their families behind with an unfillable emptiness? He wants his people to change.

Maybe if he were an omega they would listen to such principles more readily. Maybe if he were an alpha he could exude his will and herd them into his line of thinking. He needs to go speak with Phainon. For the sake of his people, he can’t let the Deliverer scent him again.

His feet carry him to Treasure of Ages as he ruminates, and, from a distance, he spots Phainon appraising antiques with intense scrutiny. The clang of his greaves against polished stone grabs his attention.

“Mydei!” he beams, placing down the amphora. “What brings you here? Excited to see me again are you?”

“Actually, I did come here to find and speak with you,” he answers and folds his arms.

“Oh.” Phainon blinks in surprise. “That’s… always an honor when you do. Do you want to join me for my lunch break?”

“Sure.”

Phainon shouts to Theodoros about his break, and invites Mydei further into the shop, sequestering into a room with a table, chairs, and countertops. Even here antiques litter throughout.

“All of these are fakes, so you don’t have to worry about breaking anything.” Phainon gestures around before digging through a basket, and pulls out fruits and dried meats.

He takes a seat by the table, watching Phainon plate his food and pour juice into a blue goblet. “You know, today I had to deliver the unfortunate news to a client about how her precious heirloom was an imitation relic and not the real thing. It's always so disheartening—I’m not fond of it, but…”

When Phainon sits beside him, his gaze lingers on him with clouded judgement, nostrils flaring subtly with irritation. His spine straightens out and his jaw sets.

“What is it?” Mydei asks.

“Nothing,” he answers too fast and focuses on his plate of food. “I have cheese if you want some.”

Mydei furrows his brow, but says nothing. Instead, he carefully picks at the grapes, making sure to not squeeze hard enough for it to burst. Phainon shifts in his seat. His leg anxiously bounces as he stuffs his face.

“Are you sure it’s nothing?” Mydei repeats his question seeing the anxiety mountain upon Phainon.

“Yes.” He nods once, tears at a piece of jerky, and chews. “It’s just—well —”

“What?”

“Why do you smell like a bunch of alphas this time?” he huffs childishly, as if the reason he smells like this is because of him. Ironically, he’s not wrong this time.

“My people were not fond of me walking around with the Deliverer’s scent,” he says.

“That’s ridiculous,” he scoffs. “What happened to the whole ‘our scents don’t matter’ rhetoric they always speak of? Surely it shouldn’t matter this much.”

“It shouldn’t,” he agrees. “But, I cannot control what they think.”

“I guess I should be honored they see me as some sort of threat when I am not,” he mutters.

“No. I wish they did not have such viewpoints. Like you said, it is nonsense.”

“Then let me scent you again. That’ll show them—” Phainon dares, then blanches into mortification over what he uttered. “I don’t say that as a means to attack you or your people. Just—Frustrated is all.”

Mydei rolls a piece of cloth between his fingers to wipe away remnants of food. His people would not approve of such a thing. They expect him to comply with the ideals they’ve set upon him. To maintain the image of the crown prince they hold dear; to be the false symbol of a home he never lived in and heard only through songs and stories.

He came here with conviction to deny such a thing from occurring again, yet he can’t bring himself to speak it into existence. Maybe, taking on his frustrated suggestion will help them understand his commitment to leading them to Okhema and not back to the ruins of what was once the marvelous city of Castrum Kremnos.

And… maybe he can enjoy the fleeting sensation of warmth tingling and prickling his skin when Phainon approaches him with a tenderness he never received in his violent past dictated by the hand of Strife.

“Go ahead,” he decides, gaze flickering to the goblet of juice as his mouth parches.

Phainon sucks in a breath and gapes. “Seriously?”

“Like I said, I don’t have issues with it.”

He breathes out a laugh, “Because you like it.”

“I take it back. You cannot scent me,” Mydei deadpans.

“Nuh-uh! No taking it back!” He pulls Mydei’s chair and brings him closer, the legs scraping against the wooden flooring. “You have to go through with your words.”

“I very much regret them.” He focuses on the table, ignoring how his ears burn.

Phainon presses against his neck once more, and his heart thuds against his ribs. Goosebumps travel along his arms at the sweet, gentle caresses. And when Phainon’s lips brush against his skin, he can feel the smile curled up at the edges. He takes his time, soaking in the sensation, breathing in whatever paltry scent he has to offer.

“Why are you so tense?” Phainon murmurs. This close, his voice sounds impossibly loud even when speaking delicately.

“I’m not tense,” he grits out, hands clenching the edges of his seat, the tips of his gauntlets leaving scratches in the wood. “I will hurl you into the wall if you continue speaking nonsense.”

Phainon’s soft chuckle provokes a shiver to travel down his spine. “My apologies. I will cease in speaking my ‘drivel’ as you so like to put it.” Another caress against his neck, and he swears Phainon puckers his lips to plant a discreet kiss. He dare not mention it. The beating of his heart against his chest pains him. “You’re not breathing though.”

“I am,” he replies almost petulantly, and remembers his body needs air in order to function.

Phainon’s shoulders tremble, and Mydei fears he might burst into laughter. His shaky hand crosses his lap to hold his exposed hip, thumb tracing the bone. A heat settles in the pit of his stomach over the warmth of his palm. Butterflies flap their wings and flutter to his throat.

“If you even think about laughing, I will destroy you,” he mutters underneath his breath, forcing down a swallow.

“Laughing? No-No, definitely not.”

“Then why are you shaking?”

“I’m not shaking.”

“Yes, you are.”

“No, I’m not.”

“You are.”

“Mydei, I will bite you if you don’t stop.”

He elbows him roughly and Phainon lets out a small, “Oof.”

But then he breaks out into a small laugh, and Mydei finds his own lips twitching upwards into a fond smile. The tension seeps away, happiness unfurling like petals greeting the sun as he accepts the added weight on him. Snow-white hair tickles his cheeks. His nose. His neck. And it feels… nice. Nice in a way he cannot place or name.

Here, hidden in the back of an antique store, he relaxes. Unwinds as Phainon still trembles in his scenting. Mydei takes in a deep breath, the smell of old papers, wood, and clay filtering through his lungs. His eyes slip shut, and he rests his head against Phainon’s crown. Phainon momentarily stiffness, the fingers upon his hip pressing into his firm muscle.

He resumes, a purr rumbling through his chest.

A foreign feeling washes over him. It is not akin to the violent piercing of arrows through his flesh. It is not similar to the gasping breaths for life as water clogs his lungs. It is not comparable to the shivering coldness which leaves his lips blue.

Mydei exhales, warmth blooming and spreading all the way down to his fingers.

It’s… nice. It brings a lightness he never experienced before. A pleasant sensation tingling up and down his spine with every caress. A nervous spike when Phainon shifts to the other side. A shaky breath when the affection returns. A squeezing of his eyes as he bites his lip.

Is this what intimacy feels like? Sudden and delicate. He fears it will shatter if he dares to press into it. So, he remains stiff as a board, unsure what to do with his hands. He tightly grasps his robes.

His people will be upset. Krateros will reprimand him. But this changes nothing between Phainon and him. There is no magical switch that makes him submit. They are equals, and everyone is daft for not understanding that. It’s just a scent he cannot sense.

He cannot… smell it. At all.

A prickling sorrow ebbs through him like a gentle tide coaxing him towards freezing waters. He thought he had grown accustomed to all pain in his life, but this is new. This leaves no wound which could be treated with a salve. No wound to cover with a bandage. No wound to right with a splint.

If he were an omega… There would be no wound at all. He would breach this unknown world, cross the threshold, and enjoy it for all it can bring. And Phainon would enjoy it more as well. It made more sense for an alpha to do this with an omega. He’s never even heard of an alpha desiring to scent a male beta.

He’d even be able to scent him back. Enjoy a closeness he never once had.

“Everything alright?” Phainon whispers as he shifts away, eyes flickering about his face in worry.

“Why wouldn’t it be?” he says, surprised over the small lump in the back of his throat, and conceals it.

“You stopped smelling like honeycakes and jam.” Phainon traces his fingers along his neck.

Mydei grips Phainon’s hand until it turns white and he winces in pain. “I told you I do not smell like a pastry.”

“Ouch! Okay, okay—can you let go of my hand? Your gauntlets really hurt!” he whimpers.

“Worry about yourself first, Deliverer,” he scoffs and releases his hand.

His tongue feels heavy inside his mouth, and he rubs it against his palette in a meager attempt to quench the dryness. He steals Phainon’s cup, and, while Phainon whines about his juice, he drinks.

It is wrong of him to do this—this scenting from an alpha. Especially when he is neither an omega or a female beta. Such things are unbecoming. He gently places the half empty cup down.

“What did you want to talk about?” Phainon asks, and he pales.

“I…” he starts, but the words lodge in his throat. Emotions begin to fray, and he takes in a deep, steadying breath. This, too, is unbecoming of him. He must contain himself.

Phainon uses his pause to resume his meal. But, when he drinks, Mydei’s eyes widen of their own volition—he drinks from the same spot he placed his lips upon.

Does he know what he’s doing? They are suddenly too close. He becomes too aware of the warmth radiating against him. Their legs touching. The lack of distance between their faces. The speckles of grey in his sky-blue eyes. The sun within his golden irises. Upturned lips stained red from pomegranate juice. The—

“Hello? Mydei?” Phainon raises his brow at him, leaning even closer. Their foreheads almost touch. He wants to close the distance. To rest his weary soul in the comfort of the Deliverer. “Are you still with me?” His voice is so pleasant. Low and melodious.

Mydei stands abruptly, gauntlets hammering against the table with a loud thud. He curls his fingers, the tips scratching the wood and collecting slivers.

“We can speak of it later,” he mutters through clenched teeth. How can he say he wishes to not be scented when he already fell?

“Oh,” Phainon eloquently says in the face of his restrained outburst. “Alright. You know I will always make time for you when you wish to speak.”

Mydei throws a vicious glare in hopes of making him cower. Instead, Phainon continues on as if nothing happened, and drinks more from the same spot again. Curse this man for acting so nonchalant. Curse him for imposing these confusing, flustered feelings upon him. A Kremnoan has no need for desiring softness. His entire being is a weapon.

“Hmph. I’ll see you around,” Mydei grumbles, trying to save face, and marches off.

“I’ll come find you during Descent Hour,” Phainon calls out. “I better not catch you napping again!”

“I’ll take back my key if you disturb me,” he threatens in return, and hears Phainon’s muffled laughter bouncing through the hall.

Mydei prepares himself for unbridled disapproval. He has placed himself in a difficult position, but perhaps he can sway the minds of his people with belligerent stubbornness. The very same stubbornness he carried with every step down the winding road of his life.

Chapter Summary

“Enough,” Mydei cuts in before Krateros has a chance to interject, before the argument devolves into vicious quarreling, “Kremnoans are prideful in their traditions, and we have always been insular. Unless you intend to challenge and defeat every willing soldier, you will not be considered as one. Even then I doubt you will be graced with the courtesy of recognition.”

Phainon scrutinizes him before asking quietly, “Is that what it will take?”

“I— What?”

“Is that what it will take?” Phainon repeats with more determination.

As he steps out towards the front of Treasure of Ages, the light from Kephale’s Dawn Device soaks him with its warm rays. He inhales a deep breath, unwinding himself from the bizarre interaction from mere moments ago. To his left, Theodoros hums and busies himself with adjusting the display painted dolias.

A tinge of guilt pinches him. He did accidentally put a few scratches and cracks into the man’s table without reason. Well, that’s not true. Much to his embarrassment, Phainon’s inappropriate behavior aggravated him to the point of acting out. Finding a priest of Oronyx to help fix his mistake becomes a high priority.

“Theodoros,” he says and approaches the man.

“Lord Mydei!” he jumps to attention. “A pleasure to see you, as always. The dolia depicting you has been selling extraordinarily well!”

The statement leaves him perplexed, but the prideful side of him basks in the unsolicited compliment. After all, he is the greatest warrior in Okhema. The Deliverer can protest the notion all he wants, but in the end he will claim victory. Just like how he’s currently ahead in their competitions.

“I wager you must assume only Kremnoans purchased the works, but I’ll have you know they’ve been quite popular with Okhemans as well.” Theodoros grins, pride etched into his words. Though, after a moment, his demeanor falters and he staggers a small step backwards.

“Is there something wrong?” Mydei asks.

“N-Not at all.” He clears his throat. “I—ah— didn’t mean to act so surprised! I— Are congratulations in order?”

“Congratulations for what?” He tries to hide his incredulousness, but his brow pinches in confusion.

“Lord Phainon’s…” He gestures vaguely, redness creeping up his cheeks then he coughs into his hand.

Ah, that’s right. Theodoros is an omega—he must be smelling Phainon’s pheromones upon him. Though, his reaction adds on to his befuddlement. Scenting is a common ritual, he shouldn’t be acting so odd.

“I wanted to tell you the table in the back has been lightly damaged. I will be requesting the services of an Oronyx priest to come and mend it, so you need not worry,” he says, deciding it best to move on with the subject and not linger.

His words have the opposite intended effect, for Theodoros’s face reddens even more and he chokes on his tongue. “I— Thank you for the kind gesture!”

“Right,” he says, he must be missing some vital piece of information for his peculiar behavior.

“You’re still here?” Phainon interrupts from behind as he steps out and parks himself beside the counter. “I didn’t realize you’d stick around because you missed me so much.”

“He… did,” he answers.

“No wonder he was so happy then.” Her features brighten to an incredible degree. “Even through all of his bluster, I can see how much you mean to him. Even if you did not know the meaning entirely, I’m sure you understood the intimacy to some extent.”

“It’s the least I can do,” he says in earnest, and escapes after they exchange farewells. There is only so much embarrassment he can handle.

This is absurd.”

The words slash Phainon, and he grimaces as he takes a step back. His breaths come out heavy and shuddering, his hands clench so tight his nails threaten to cut open his skin and drip golden ichor.

“I’m not an omega for you to scent,” Mydei gently says, reminding himself of a bond he can never have for he never will be. “Nor am I an alpha who can contest the declaration of being scented. As the crown prince, I must stand on these principles. With that you must understand our differences.”

“I see.” Phainon purses his quivering lip, and takes in a deep breath through his nose. “You have been brainwashed into believing such things because you are ignorant, and wish to remain as such without consulting me.”

“I am anything but ignorant,” he defends himself.

“I know it's not my place to act as your advisor on these matters, but your understanding is primitive and follows traditions, for that is what you’ve been taught by others.” Phainon grips the strap upon his chest holding his pauldron, and tugs at it.

“Why must you make everything so difficult?” Mydei groans. He knew this conversation was going to be unpleasant, but he never anticipated such a strong reaction. “If anything, you scenting my neck instead of my wrists is what brought this upon us.”

“I’m not making things difficult,” he petulantly responds. “I’m making a statement—one I observe as a fact. And the other thing I’m observing is how much of a coward Mydeimos is.”

“Excuse me?” This insult he did not expect.

“Indeed.” Phainon grabs his wrist, and he tries to tug away. “Instead of finding a solution, you decide to run away with your tail between your legs. Unless you forget—which I believe you haven’t—you enjoyed it. So why shouldn’t I fight for it? I know it's what you want.”

“Unhand me, Deliverer,” Mydei growls in their tug of war, his frightful strength digging through the hard metal of his gauntlet, pressuring and squeezing his wrist.

He throws fist against Phainon’s head in an attempt to dislodge himself. Phainon dodges with ease.

“Or what? You’ll defeat me in a battle? Need I remind you of our equal strength,” Phainon taunts him.

His heart skips a beat at the reminder, and his blood burns. Punches and kicks are thrown, blows are parried, and bruises are given. Their exertions convey what words cannot; the language of combat speaks of desperation in Phainon. The frustration of being denied and how it boils him leaves his stance wide and full of holes. The exhaustion plaguing him slows his movements.

“You will listen.” Mydei cracks his forehead against the alpha’s, pain splintering through his skull towards the back of his head.

“I only listen to Mydei,” Phainon grunts as he wraps his arms around Mydei’s torso, securing his hold with a tight grip.

“Idiot, I am Mydei,” he grunts out through gritted teeth.

Phainon hunches down and presses forward, using all of his strength to push him down onto the ground and air knocks out of his lungs. Mydei glares up at him as they both heave. Phainon holds him down by the shoulders, and a red bruise blooms on his forehead.

“You…” Phainon starts, sun eclipsing the sky-blue expanse, and a wild grin stretches across him. A familiar, uncomfortable heat settles itself in his groin. They’re close. Close enough for warm puffs of breath to ghost upon his face. “Looks like I’ve scented you again by sheer proximity this time. Won’t people be upset?”

“They… will be,” he mutters, plopping his head against the ground in defeat. “Phainon, I…”

Phainon lets go of his shoulders, and leans further down to rest his weight against his elbows. They are so close like this, chests almost flush. He can feel his heat engulfing his exposed skin. He bites the inside of his cheek in an attempt to quell the confused fluttering of his heart. They were never this close before, and he has no idea where it comes from.

“I don’t want to give this up,” Phainon murmurs so quietly he wonders if he is meant to hear the confession. “It won’t matter that I do this since you already have my scent upon you, and it's quite late into Parting Hour.”

He presses himself up against his scent glands, and Mydei’s breathing stutters. It's soft, gentle. Just like how he remembers. The will to fight saps from his bones, and he lays heavy against the dirt. Vines wrap around his limbs, gripping him into submission, feeding upon his strength with greedy gulps. He gives in, allowing Phainon to caress him. Allows him to pour himself over.

He wonders if he even has the courage to shove him off if his frustrations willed it. But this warmth, this closeness, it intoxicates him. Makes him wish to wrap an arm around him and close the tiny distance between them. To feel Phainon’s weight upon him, and ground him to the earth underneath.

Mydei exhales a shuddering breath.

“You don’t need to worry,” Phainon whispers against his ear, and his toes curl as his groin pulses with desire. “No one will know.”

“I will,” he says, and finds the roughness of his voice surprising.

Phainon leans up, and their noses almost brush. “The only one who matters.”

Close—too close! Strength surges through him, and he shoves Phainon off. He hears him laughing over the loud thudding of his heart. Ah, how it thrashes and bewilders him. Mydei rubs his chest underneath his bulky necklace, trying to calm it down.

Phainon lays beside him, pleased and quiet. A soft breeze rustles shrubberies and trees around them. No sounds of sparring, chatter, or footsteps interrupt the intimate air. They are here—alone. And Mydei melts from knowing his lonesomeness is broken by the Deliverer’s ceaseless persistence.

“Mydei,” Phainon breaks the silence after a few beats.

“What?”

“I’m not going to let this go.”

He dryly chuckles. “Why did I hope you’d let this be easy for me? Fine. I cannot dictate your actions, but I do not approve of them.”

Mydei shifts to look at Phainon, and his eyes widen as he realizes the other is already watching him with ardent determination.

“That’s fine. I don’t need your approval for this. I apologize in advance if it causes you trouble.”

And he can’t fight the smile tugging at his lips. Warmth invades his core, seeping its way through his chest and up his ears. But spikes of anxiety wedge between the spaces of his ribs for indulging these soft desires. He’s no omega, he should not be enjoying the presence of an alpha, for how can an alpha ever feel the same for a beta? They share no special, intrinsic bond.

He’s so close. If he willed it, he could outstretch his hand and reach forward —touch the rays of sunlight breaking through the darkness of the bottomless sea he lives in. Breach the surface and gasp in air his lungs burn for.

He sits instead.

“Don’t get full of yourself, Deliverer,” he scoffs in his bluster. “You act as if I want such a thing. I’d be more pleased if you stayed beside yourself.”

“I can’t afford to this time,” he says with a small, humorless laugh.

Mydei moves to stand, but Phainon grips his wrist, halting his action.

“Can—Can we stay for a little while longer… Please?” His question borders on begging.

And Mydei… always has a hard time denying him.

“Fine. But I’ll be leaving after a quint,” he huffs as if it’s some terrible inconvenience. Allows himself to be yanked back down to the ground.

Because the smile Phainon gives is always, always worth it. Every single time. And if they sit closer than they usually do, pressing their shoulders together, heads tilted towards one another, he’ll keep it to himself.

“That’s-!” Castorice’s face flushes instantly, transcending her pale features into something akin to blood soaking through linen bandages. “Lord Mydei, why don’t we forgo reading that one?”

“Is there something wrong with it?” he asks dryly. Ever since he began his venture into reading romantic novels, Castorice waxed and waned between eagerness and apprehensiveness. Her fingers wiggle in desperation as she inches closer to take the scroll from him.

“There’s nothing necessarily wrong with it,” she squeaks and scoots back before she gets too close. “I don’t think it is a variety you will appreciate.”

While he has no issues talking about the biological matters of sexual intercourse, reading the more flowery language describing the acts of “thrusting” and “slick drenched loins” leaves him absolutely flustered. The first time he happened upon such a thing, he startled like a newborn fawn, tried to get through a few sentences, then clasped it shut as steam rose from his head.

Unfortunately for him, most works have a fascination for heat and rut cycles; they create entire plots and genres where protagonists have to deal with impulsivity, going as far as to make one of the reasons they get together being through the lens of “assisting” one another in the name of either friendship or convenience. He tried so hard to stomach such stories, but the second the narration heated up, he sped across the text, running away from the impending shyness enveloping him, until he couldn't take it anymore and closed it.

Instead, he explained in a calm, demure fashion that he harbored no desire to continue reading such works. The last thing he wants to do is upset her.

However, whispers flood his mind over this unique premise. They nudge him towards a possibility he never considered, begging for this reality to be true. “Can such a thing even exist?”

“It’s a work of pure fiction. It can’t actually happen.” She exhales a shaky breath as she clutches her chest.

“I’ll return it then.” He stands, and allows her privacy to recollect herself.

A hollow sadness envelops him as he walks towards the shelves where he found it. Delicately, he slides the scroll back into its proper place, and gazes about the section once more. Being Aglaea’s library, she has a treasure trove of romantic literature, but no matter how hard he searched, he couldn’t find anything else playing upon the coupling of an alpha and a male beta.

This story was the only one, and even it transforms the beta into an omega.

Maybe they were destroyed in the homelands of other city-states as citizens ran away from the plaguing black tide. He traces the shelves, fingers bumping against the indents of wood, metal, and parchments, and picks one out at random.

Another alpha and omega coupling. Another perfect, harmonious bonding. Another slice to the gaping, festering wound he bears. And he wonders why it matters to him at all. Why such a fact leaves him anxious and saddened. Even though he wonders, he does not dwell; he cannot dwell. He pinches such feelings between his fingers, and nestles them deep within, and forgets they ever existed.

He inserts the scroll back, and returns to Castorice who has now composed herself.

“Welcome back,” she smiles as if their earlier conversation never happened, “I think you’ll like this one.” She hands him a new piece, sliding it across the table like always, and he unfurls it. “It’s a fluffy piece—it goes into about nesting and what makes it special to both the omega and alpha.”

She grins in her excitement, swinging her feet underneath her chair. “I quite like that one a lot. It’s very cute and elicits so many soft emotions.”

Historical texts are his preferred readings, for he can learn through them and apply himself to become a better leader.
