“I thought you had more fight in you, Deliverer,” he jeers in gleeful bliss.

Phainon lets out a heartfelt laugh, panting as sweat drips down his brow, and sets on with fierce determination.

To say he intended to lose would be a lie. He truly did intend to escape the Deliverer’s pursuit. However, as he turns sharply from a sprint, the ground picks up against his heel and he skids, losing his balance, and crashes face first into a weapons rack. The wooden beams snap from the sudden impact of force, and weapons scatter all around. Phainon, never one to lose an opportunity, lunges at him, crashes down on him like a tidal wave, pinning him into place between his thighs.

“I win,” Phainon boasts, low and deep, something on the edge of a growl, and Mydei shudders.

Fingers dance across his sides. He squirms and struggles as his body betrays him and he laughs. Laughs, laughs, and laughs. His stomach aches, tears sting the corners of his eyes, and he swears he will kill Phainon for agonizing him in such a way. His body is a weapon, meant for suffering wounds and death for others, not to glimmer and glow with joy!

Phainon’s tickling eases, his gaze turning serene as he watches him laugh so readily.

Mydei surges forward, pushing Phainon off balance and forward until his back thuds against the ground. He looms overhead, clasping his wrists against the ground, and straddling his stomach, panting heavily as he catches his breath. His chiton slips off his shoulders, hanging by his elbow and exposes more of his skin. Phainon pants in turn, his face flush a crimson red, wild eyes flitting about his face, neck, and chest. His canines protrude far more than normal, fully unsheathed and on display for him to see.

It is wrong to enjoy such an expression on him; to imagine how painful his bite would be upon his nape. How his blood would flow.

Phainon, beneath him like this, heaving for air, snow-white hair splayed and a mess, is a different sight to behold.

“Mydei, you are so…” Phainon starts, and he prepares for a jab to come, to disperse the intimate air.

He wants to memorize this image, imprint it into the core of his soul, pull out a photostone and capture a picture, whatever it will take to never forget. Before Phainon ruins it. Because the sight before him is so… is so…

He swallows. A fuzziness permeates in the air, tickling his nose and clinging to the back of his throat.

He is so…

Beautiful.

“Beatiful…” Phainon breathes, uttering the word like a confession.

The two freeze up; Mydei stares as a hum of static fills his ears, and Phainon’s eyes go wide as he chokes on his tongue, strangling him from saying anything else. He shoots up, shoving Mydei off.

An awkward beat passes, and he glares a hole into the ground, jaw set so tight a muscle pulses, fingers clawing into the dirt as he clenches them into fists. Tiny pebbles dig into his palms, grounding him back to reality.

“I—Uh—” Phainon rubs the back of his head, bringing up his knees to his chest. “I think I’ll go and get some of that rest you spoke of.”

He says nothing in response. Phainon shuffles to his feet, and scampers off, glancing back only once across his shoulder. Mydei’s tongue twists upon itself, his heart continues its erratic drumming, and no air enters his lungs.

A warmth spreads through him like dim embers of a hearth stoked by the shifting of charcoal, encouraged by the soft blowing of wind until a fire sparks within and grows. So uncontainable it is, he sits for a long while, feeling it engulf every extremity and spread to his ears.

So still he is, a nymph mistakes him for a marbled statue, and climbs across his leg, snapping him out of his stupor. With a gentle touch, he brushes the beetle away, and releases the sigh held within. He’s been called many curses, many slanders, and many critiques before.

But never an adoration so delicately whispered in reverence for him; the one who committed patricide and left a slew of wars in his wake. As he returns home, he crosses his arms, hiding how his hands tremble. Hiding, even from himself, how his spirit rises and touches the sky itself.

Yet he sleeps so well this night. Curled up in his bed surrounded by a multitude of plush pillows—face buried into one as he clutches it—and dreams of Phainon chasing him again. And when he catches him, he presses him down against the earth, and kisses him instead, fingers intertwined.

☼

Dangerous, he decides and furrows his brow, Phainon is dangerous. He draws inexplicable fantasies, probing his untouchable wound with the sharp tip of his quill. The jet black ink seeps through the cracks, rewriting everything he knew about the alpha. Trianne walks alongside him in his patrolling, peering at him with curiosity every so often.

An omega Kremnoan soldier stands, ready for any sign of the black tide, alongside an Okheman guard. They glare at one another, throw snide remarks as if it were a sport, and Mydei ignores their bickering where he would normally intercept to maintain a peace.

“What’s wrong, De?” Trianne asks, “You look like something is troubling you. Is it because Snowy is fighting?”

Has he really become so easy to read? The thought unnerves him.

“No, I’m not worried about him,” he says as evenly as he can.

“But you’re scowling so much.”

“I’m not.”

“He’ll be okay,” Trianne assures, “Snowy is strong when he puts his mind to something.”

“That’s not—” he sighs, and leads her towards a side of the building, climbing the stairs nestled against it for a good vantage of the block. “I’m not worried about whether he will lose. I know he is more than capable.”

“Oh.” She presses a finger against her chin. “Then what is it?”

A familiar sense of unease creeps through him. Kremnoans move throughout the blocks designated by Aglaea as high risks, their coordinated strides bringing calm through familiarity, yet talking to Trianne about his worries make sure it lingers.

He rests his palms against the bannister, and says, “Even though Phainon may be a strong warrior, he has been neglecting himself. Proper maintenance of both body and mind is important, yet he rejects it in his mindless pursuit. I know he has been neglecting sleep.”

Trianne nods thoughtfully. “He has always been like that when he has something he focuses on. It used to be worse in the past, and he’s gotten better with it.”

“I don’t see why he won’t give it a rest,” he heaves a sigh. “Scenting me is not so important for him to duel every single Kremnoan.”

“I don’t think he views it that way,” Trianne softly says. “You are important to him. Ever since you’ve come to Okhema, he has gradually improved to be what he is now. Maybe, to him, it’s an attack on your bond he wants to protect.” Then, almost teasingly, she continues, “Not everyone can stuff their feelings down like you, De.”

“I’m not stuffing away my feelings.” He scowls, though her words echo through his head, bringing a clarity to a subject he desperately wants to ignore.

“You always come to the conclusion of isolating yourself to be the right path when it’s not. And you always look so happy when you are with him,” Trianne offers her gentleness, coaxing him out of his tension.

He remembers such a happiness once, when his five companions were still alive. How they sat around campfires in the late nights, spinning tales, laughing amongst one another until one by one their group dwindled and he alone remained.

“Sometimes it is,” he murmurs. “For the sake of peace I alone can handle burdens no one else can. This curse of immortality makes it so.”

“What does your curse have to do with Snowy wanting to be close with you?” she asks with a tilt of her head.

“I…” And ties his tongue. He can answer he does not wish to outlive the Deliverer, but such a thing matters not. The prophecy foretold that Phainon alone would witness the miracle of Era Nova. He will make it to the end. Where he will end up he does not know.

“How about we make Snowy a pie to cheer him on?” She grins in her delight. “You promised us to bake, so let's do something nice to make Snowy happy. Maybe if he feels like you support his efforts he will be so relaxed he can sleep.”

The idea… doesn’t sound half bad. Though, presenting a hand made pie with the three Tribbies brings an ounce of embarrassment, but with them around, he can cover his real intentions. And he knows how the Deliverer will brighten as if he handed him the sun. The image stokes a warmth within, and a soft smile crests his lips. Maybe then, he will finally listen.

“I suppose that’s not a bad idea.”

“Yeah.” She grins and giggles. “He’ll be so shocked and touched. What kind of—”

A crash explodes from the other side of the street. Roof shillings, and stone flies, colliding into the ground, and cracking apart. Tapestries tear apart. A pillar topples over, and the crowd around the vicinity scream and panic. Abominable black tide monsters slither through, slashing and swiping with reckless abandon, leaving a wake of black in their paths.

Mydei snaps to attention, and shouts commands to his fellow soldiers who jump to their feet.

“Lady Trianne, help the civilians escape,” he orders, and she flies to do her part.

He charges forth, clashing with a Tide-Eroded Blade that whirls its edged arms with intent to kill, and the corruption seeps through into his skin. The civilians within the area follow Trianne’s orders as she zips about and leads them to safety.

It slashes his torso, and his golden blood flows out of the freshly made wound. He takes the opportunity to land several blows upon it, breaking and chipping at its blackened construction. The sun upon its head glows with pain, whirring in frustration.

An Okheman guard finds purchase with her blade as Mydei distracts it, delivering a devastating slash across its back. And another guard follows her example, striking with firm resolution. He whirls a kick as the creature stumbles, bisecting it in half.

However, no moment can be spared as another burst of black tide creature erupts.

Mydei spots those two omegas from the markets—the one he felt a needless rage towards as they cooed over Phainon—cowering underneath a fallen stall. A Corroded Axe rushes towards them, eager to kill and spread chaos. They scream in terror as they grip one another, tears pouring down their faces as they pray for salvation.

Without thinking, he intercepts the charge, the black axe the monster wields cleaves through his shoulder to his sternum, and he grips it tight to hold it in place. Golden blood floods his lungs and throat, he hacks it out and strains to maintain his hold.

“Go!” He orders the omegas, but they are too paralyzed in fear. “Run!”

The creature tries to pull back its weapon for another slice. An arrow from a Black Tide Decrepit Bow whizzes past and the girls scramble to the left as they clutch one another. Another arrow pierces his shoulder and blood drips, drips, drips.

A coldness blooms from his tenth thoracic vertebrae, flowing through to his extremities, and his vision blurs. When he opens his eyes, the familiar river greets him once more like a spurned old friend. Souls travel down the current, following the west wind, seeking where it ends.

But he cannot follow, for there is still so much to do. So much to fight for. So many regrets he will leave in the world of the living if he lets go.

One step after another, he trudges against the current, pain wracking through his body, tearing him apart with every stride. His golden soul glows from exertion, and he focuses on what he still must do. His people need to be led to a better life and treated as proper citizens. He needs to defeat his maddened god and return the coreflame of Strife for the Flame-Chase journey. Strength pours through him, and he reaches forward as light sparks through his vision once more.

He needs to assure Phainon he will always love him no matter what comes between them. No matter how many deaths he suffers through. No matter who or what tries to separate them.

His heart accelerates, pumping blood through his veins, and lifeforce surges through his spine, plugging his soul back into his body.

When he comes to, a roar rips through his lungs and throat, grasps the creature by its arm, presses a foot against its chest—and pulls. The limb cracks and frays as it tries to dislodge him. Tries to fight against his strength. With a sickening snap, he tears it asunder. The axe lodged within his shoulder begins to dissipate as the creature stumbles back. In a joint effort, Kremnoan and Okheman soldiers bring death to the creature.

A glob of blood coats his mouth, and he spits it out before righting himself with haggard breaths. The soldiers around him celebrate the victory. Shrill exultations of the omegas behind him grabs his attention.

“We’re alive!” one exclaims as she holds her friend by the shoulders. “Lord Mydei saved us.”

The other one cries and cries, not having come to the sudden calm around her.

“Don’t cry now, we’re alive,” she says, and wipes her friend's tears away with a thumb.

And his eyes widen as she kisses her full on the lips, leaving him gaping. The other omega buries her face into her shoulder.

“Thank you, Lord Mydei,” she says to him.

“You two… are together?” he says. Blood loss always leaves him delirious, and he worries in believing his vision.

“We are,” a breathy laugh escapes her, tears stinging the corners of her eyes.

“How? You two are omegas. You are supposed to be with alphas.”

She strokes her lover’s hair, her own hand trembles in the soothing gesture. A small laugh escapes her as she says, “That may be what others want from us, but we don’t follow tradition.”

Blood gurgles through his lungs as his body begins the arduous process of healing. And a coughing fit envelopes him. These two omegas who left him in a confused, trembling rage had no interest in the Deliverer this entire time. His mind created scenarios which did not exist, and upset him so.

Golden ichor splats onto his palm, freeing him of the drowning within; the pattern evokes memories of his debased actions, of the thoughts which brought him across the threshold to life, of his dreams he pretended did not exist. Of the warm, comforting fire only Phainon could bring. Of the rays of light he wishes to grasp. How they illuminate the darkness of the river he sinks and suffocates in.

Oh.

Aquila's wings freeze in the sky, rushing rivers stall, and the lion stills in its hunt of the oryx. The world comes to a halt as if blessed by Oronyx themselves, allowing him a precious moment to realize. To let it fall into place.

Oh.

He’s in love.

Distracted by his new found revelation, he does not recall Trinnon holding his hand and leading him to a clinic. His head flies in the clouds as his wounds are dressed by a doctor. His healing factor works and aches his muscles as they stitch together, and his body itches deep through his layers of flesh. Thankfully, no casualties are reported, and he relaxes at the success.

He lays on the kline, staring at the ceiling above, as he allows this newfound feeling to settle and hum. How could he not see such a simple thing before? In hindsight, it glared in its blinding truth. But, even as it percolates, doubt continues to shadow him. Is a beta allowed to fall in love with an alpha?

Can a beta ever compare to an omega whose entire being molds for the alpha and the same in return? He stands as an outcast to these dynamics, lost to their language of love. He may wield great power as a prince, but he lacks experience of gentle desires. All he has known, and will ever know, is violence.

The other wounded Kremnoan and Okheman soldiers rest across from him, and for once, their conversations do not drift to arguments and curses. They boast of their combat prowess, and dismantling the black tide creatures together.

The omega from before enters after a gentle knock against the door, bearing a calathus of pomegranates in her arms and a sheepish smile.

“Lord Phainon told us these are your favorite,” she says. “We wanted to give you a proper thanks for saving us.”

“... Thank you.” He takes it from her. The fruits jostle and settle into place. “Where is your… lover?” The word tastes odd on his tongue.

“She’s recovering from the shock of it all,” the omega answers with a smile.

He stares at the fruit, head still fuzzy from blood loss, and asks, “Does it not bother you that she’s not an alpha? From what I understand, an alpha and omega are meant for each other as a bonded pair, yet you give it up. Is that really okay?”

The omega blinks at his spilling of words, then bursts out into laughter. “You and Lord Phainon are truly similar for asking the same question. Of course it is okay, we love one another.” She places a hand upon her chest, and a reverent smile graces her. “I can’t imagine giving myself up for an alpha simply because it is what is expected of me and being told it is right.”

“Phainon has asked something similar?” He perks up in curiosity, and a hope he never wished to foster, glows.

“Maybe it is best for you to ask him,” she says as if she knows the answers to all of his questions.

The thought of asking something so forward terrifies him. These feelings should never be known, but the look she gives urges him to throw such thoughts away. And perhaps he should stop being such a coward, running away because they are new and never before felt. He has fought creatures of the deep, endured the onslaught of armies, yet these simple human interactions terrify him so.

In a fight, he knows what to expect. In dealing with Phainon he may as well be a lost pup digging through sand in hopes of finding treasure.

Yet, Phainon is the one who fights for their bond while he runs away. Braves the thundering storm as it bashes him with hail and burns him with lightning for days on end without shelter. How can he consider himself a man when he cannot stand beside the Deliverer and offer his support?

The crown prince of Castrum Kremnos cannot know fear. He is resolute in his resolve. Steadfast in all of his actions.

And so, in this quiet clinic, he comes to this: he will show his open, selfish support for Phainon. Fight alongside him in this battle not meant for spear or sword. His people live in days of old, and he pushes for the new, and this will be another example of such.

☼

After the doctor approves of his leave, on his return to the arena where Phainon continues his battles, he encounters a Kremnoan father and son who grab his attention. He knows them well, for they are the elder and youth who traveled with the original detachment; the time when they bore no Kremnoan flag and had yet to defeat his father.

Now the elder’s wrinkles have deepened, and the youth has grown into adulthood. They exchange a few pleasantries before one speaks up.

“Your highness,” the elder omega, Milo, says, “It is a shame you have an alpha fight for you with such ardence, yet you refrain from showing support.”

“Of course he doesn’t,” his alpha son, Lampros, interrupts. “This is no Kremnoan Festival, but a classic show of Okheman pageantry.”

Milo chuckles, years of wisdom laced through in the way he shakes his head. “This is no pageantry. It is a fight for what he believes in, and isn’t that the most honorable way to show what you stand for? No waiting for a festival, and showing urgency for what matters.”

“Do you despise Phainon for what he is?” Mydei abruptly asks, and the two raise their brows in surprise.

“No,” Lampros’s voice raises in shock, “There are many of us who disagree with how this ordeal is playing itself out. We don’t need the alpha Phainon making a show of Kremnoan weakness by defeating so many of us.”

“And, many of us don’t need such extravagance to see how much he cares for you. He has already proven himself worthy in your first bout with him,” Milo adds on.

Mydei’s lip quirks up of its own volition, and their admissions leaves him light.

“I have been too consumed in thought to see what is right in front of me,” he says. “Your words are a kindness to hear, thank you.”

“Don’t thank us! Just get him to stop so he can finish embarrassing us,” Lampros cringes while Milo laughs heartily.

“And show him your support. That poor lad looks like he’s about to collapse at any moment.”

“I will.” Mydei stirs with conviction, and marches forward with steadfast steps.

For too long has he cowered in the shadows of tradition. Shielding himself with it in protection from these newborn feelings of romantic love, ones he has never experienced before. No more, he decides, pace increasing as he strides past the hollering market sellers, past the bickering screams about inventory, and past the laughing women sharing in their gossip. No more.

And light crests his vision as he enters the training grounds, no longer hiding behind pillars and lurking in the shadows. His people separate to create a path, and he steps forward to the front.

A metal greatsword arcs through the air, spinning erratically until it stabs itself through the earth upright, the hilt a splintered, crushed mess.

“Yield,” Krateros orders, the tip of his blade pointing at Phainon’s forehead who stares up with widened eyes and heaving manic breaths.

The crowd behind him erupts. The earth quakes underneath the stomping of their feet. The wind reverberates with a cacophony of piercing cheers and whistles. The light reflects off the bladed edge as it gleams in victory. Excitement sways and dances around him, goading him to join in the celebration, yet he stands petrified before it all.

And vehement desperation carves itself upon Phainon’s visage as he loses, to the ovation of all.

Mydei needs to act. Now. Before the situation dissolves into a mess. Phainon’s glare screams he’s about to act on a reckless desire; the thunderous cheer dims to a quieter celebration, spreading as eager chattering about the concluded duel.

But how can he act? Thoughts of violence spring to his mind—a duel, a ravage pummeling, snapping that sword in twain—for this is his heritage, but he hates the senseless violence it brings. He can scoff at this display, leave Phainon to fend for himself at the turn of his heel. After all, he is the one who decided on this course of action no matter his disapproval. Or he can accept the outcome of Krateros’s victory, decree it and let Phainon deal with the repercussions of his actions.

The crowd’s attention shifts to him, and his skin prickles underneath their scrutiny. They wait for his reaction; wait for the crown prince to speak. Phainon turns in confusion, and the whites of his eyes become clear as panic overtakes him.

And it settles upon him: he never wants the Deliverer to look at him in such a desperate way again.

“Everyone has witnessed your defeat,” Krateros begins, stowing his blade at the side of his hip. “You will honor what you have wagered in the loss of your contention. You will not approach crown prince Mydeimos anymore.” And adds with a sneer, “You will not delude him with opulent luxuries of your master or your beguiling alpha ways.”

Irritation snaps through Mydei, searing through his veins and roiling his blood. Phainon opens his mouth to voice his contention, and Mydei storms towards the fray. He cannot stand there, mouth agape like a child.

“Have these games finally come to an end?” he says, distaste dripping through every word and pooling into a dark tide underneath his feet. He stands above Phainon, noting the bruises upon his exposed arms. “Have you all finally beaten the Deliverer to your satisfaction? Voiced your discontent with him and Okhema?”

A hush falls upon the audience, and Krateros’s jaw flexes in the gritting of his teeth.

“This farce has gone long enough,” Mydei crosses his arms and scowls.

“Farce—!?” Phainon startles.

He silences him with a glare, and Phainon snaps his mouth shut. Though, he twitches, fingers scraping and heels digging against the ground. And Mydei prays he listens, to have his trust in what he is about to say.

With a reluctant sigh, Phainon holds his tongue and rises to his feet. Mydei takes the place by his side, where he wishes to be most, and Phainon gently amazes for it.

“I should have put an end to it before it even began. Phainon has been my equal since the day we met—since the first night of our ten day duel to the death,” he continues steadily, gaze drifting through the crowd until it settles on Krateros. “This excuse to exercise a form of revenge against him has festered and grown into mindless strife. Perpetuated by a false cause, exacerbated by the Deliverer himself who only desired to be treated as an equal; as one of us. A desperation bred from the faults of ourselves.”

Krateros speaks with urgency, “Mydeimos, the rules of these duels have already been established by all. You can’t—”

“I can,” Mydei interrupts him. “I, as crown prince of Castrum Kremnos, hereby decree the outcome of this duel invalid. It never held merit to begin with, and was an excuse for senseless violence.”

The crowd gasps, and rumbles with hushed opinions. His ears perk up from whispers all around, yet he focuses his gaze on Krateros.

“And if anyone wishes to contest my judgement, they are welcome to try me,” he concludes, and gestures with his head for Phainon to follow.

“What is the meaning of this, Mydeimos,” Krateros hisses in disdain, “to come right on the eve of his defeat and bail him out of what he could not succeed in?”

“Like I said,” he says, and yanks the greatsword out of the ground, then tosses it to Phainon who disappears it in a shower of sparks, “if anyone takes issue with this outcome, they are free to try and best me in a duel.” He bites back the comment of knowing the forgone conclusion of his victory.

Krateros studies him with a cool gaze, the fists at his sides trembling in their white knuckled clenching. Phainon follows after him, head kept low as bangs shadow his eyes, and he strides through the parting crowd.

Murmurs surround them. Some of bemusement, some of anger, and barely any of approval. He does not know what the consensus will be by the end of the day, but he does know wild tales will be spun. As they always are.

They continue on towards his house, but Phainon's footsteps whisper against the ground, and he worries the alpha lost his way and drifted off. Yet, he does not turn around to confirm if he remains, for doing so will make him appear weak in his determination.

Only when he thrusts the door open with a forceful swing does he allow himself to look back, and relief floods through him at seeing Phainon, even if his head hangs low and his disposition bleak.

“Did you finally get it all out of your system?” he asks after ushering Phainon inside.

“You're hurt,” Phainon says instead.

He thumbs at the bandages dressed across his shoulders and torso. They are unnecessary for the wounds underneath have healed, but he let the doctor worry over him to soothe his fretful ego.

“I heard of it earlier today,” Phainon continues, his tone tinges with panic then laces with bitterness. “And I couldn't do anything to stop it.”

“The wounds have already healed,” he assures as he always does whenever Phainon agonizes over his health.

“Did you die?” Phainon presses.

Even through his pale visage, the darkness underneath his eyes, the hunch of exhaustion tugging him down, he worries for his health. Still holds Mydei's immortal life like it's meant to be cherished, and not sacrificed. It frustrates him.

“I did,” he answers with an unusual amount of reluctance.

Phainon inhales sharply, and holds it deep within his chest. “I should've been there— You wouldn't have died if I were.” He groans and clutches his head as he agonizes. “But this is—was important too! If only I could split myself in two, make another copy of myself or something then I—”

“Enough.” Mydei grasps his arm and yanks so hard he almost topples over. He drags the Deliverer towards the private bath in his dwelling; one afforded to him as a royal gift from Aglaea. A fountain in the shape of a seashell affixed to the wall flows warm water into the small pool, though it lacks Phagousa’s blessing, and cycles through a drain allowing it to always remain fresh.

“Strip.”

“Excuse me?”

“You will clean yourself and rest. I've had enough of your recklessness.”

“Oh.” There’s that tick of his brow, the one where he is frustrated and looking to fight. “So you get to be the one to tell me what I—”

“Strip,” he repeats with a condescending sneer, having little patience for Phainon's attitude. “Or I will do it myself.”

Phainon glowers in return, calculating the worth of the argument. He stands there, deliberating to himself while Mydei procures an extra set of evening clothing for the alpha to change into once done.

When he returns, he thanks Kephale seeing Phainon soaking in the pool of water. He places the clothes to the side, grabbing a wash cloth to help scrub the Deliverer’s back, strips himself of his boots and settles at the ledge, the water soaking his calves.

“I should be the one taking care of you,” Phainon murmurs, wrapping his arms around his legs and tucking his chin between his knees.

And when that subtle scent of sweetness grows, he finds himself encouraged by it. How such a small, comforting gesture can soothe him.

"What's wrong, Deliverer?" he asks in a soft, tender voice, rubbing at his back, wanting to ease his woes.

Phainon's breath hitches, and the hold upon him tightens. Fingertips ghost across his back until the flat of his palm rests on top of his weak spot. He presses his hand down on it, as if protecting it, but then his thumb strokes the skin above it, as if apologizing.

"I'm so tired."

"Then rest," he says and squeezes. The weight of Phainon leans on him further, and he holds him steady.

"I can't," he whispers in a course voice. "I need to find a way to save us all."

"You will. If there is anyone who can, it is you," he assures, confident in his words.

Phainon breathes out a ragged sigh. His scent easing to a crackling hearth of home. "You always have such confidence in me. Never once do you doubt what I must do."

Mydei raises a hand, threads it through his snow-white hair, scratching down his scalp in a comforting gesture. It must work, for Phainon leans into him more. Sweat prickles and forms as the scorching heat of his body envelops him. "You are my equal. Whatever you are going through, I will not turn away."

Phainon begins to nip at his neck, his hot breath ghosting along the expanse, but stops himself. Disallows the pleasure of the gesture he uses for comfort. Instead, he pulls away. Smokey wisps trail from the corners of his eyes.

“Deliverer what has happened in the short time I left Okhema?” he presses, grasping his arms before he can pull away completely. "Speak to me."

“In three years we will meet again,” he says and pries his hands off no matter how hard he clenches. “And I apologize for such a thing.”

"What are you talking about?" Mydei asks, a crack of desperation seeping through.

"Go home, Mydei. Enjoy your people, your companions, and..." His gaze drifts away, leaving his final word unsaid. "Cherish what you can until the time comes. Do that for me. Please."

The Deliverer turns to the cliffside, and walks. Mydei tries to get more answers from him, but he remains silent as he approaches the ledge. His feet do not stop. He continues, and falls.

Mydei dashes.

"Phainon!" he yells as he grasps the edge of the cliff, steeling against the vicious vertigo as he beholds the empty air and tall trees beneath.

No sign of him remains. A subtle breeze rustles leaves as his eyes dart around in their search. Disbelief overtakes him. Perhaps it was an illusion, a trick from Zagreus to mess with his emotions he tries to convince himself again. But it felt so real. No magic could replicate his alpha to such a startling degree.

An arrow pierces the back of his chest, and he curses underneath his breath as he tears it through him to be free of it. He still has more cleanup to do and can't spare any more moments to ponder over Phainon's strange appearance and disappearance.

The next strike he lands against the black tide creature is particularly vicious.

When he returns to Okhema, he ignores the greetings of his people, the curious glances and glares from Okhemans. He races straight towards Treasure of the Ages and cannot find Phainon there. He runs to the baths, searching every pool and bench for the man. It is only by a spared glance towards the rooftops does he spot Phainon sitting at his favorite spot in Marmoreal Market and relief floods through him.

He sits there, legs dangling off the roof, gazing at the distant Dawn Device with a rather bored expression.

He makes his winding way up towards the rooftop, breathless from his constant sprinting, and calls out to him.

Phainon turns, the brightness of the Dawn Device glimmering in his eyes. His lips stretch from a pensive purse into a wide grin. "There you are! You know, you should really check your teleslate more often. Did you seriously go on an expedition on your own for a couple of days without inviting me? I didn't take you to be so afraid of losing to me in a contest."

And in this moment, he sees the two images of Phainon overlap, yet their countenance tremendously differ. There is no misery etched into every facet of his being, no desolation coloring his words grim. Three years he said. Three years until what?

"Why are you looking at me like that?" Phainon asks in worry as he stands; the steady push of palms against the roof tiles, the way his back bends and straightens. It's all the same. "Is everything alright?"

Is it three years of time he can share with Phainon until the wheel of fate turns and prophecies take hold? One alone shall witness the Era Nova, and he knows he will not be there to witness it. They will not welcome the new world together. All he can do is pray they will meet again in a peaceful life.

"Sweetheart?" he stands close now, face to face, his sky-blue eyes searching his features for an answer.

And Mydei takes a hold of his face, surging forward into a messy kiss. Phainon stumbles a step back in surprise before wrapping his arms around him to hold steady. Mydei grips his hips, and leads him until his back presses against the wall, and he does not let up in his affections. He bites at his bottom lip, pulling at it before he opens his mouth and Phainon's tongue meets his.

A heavy ache weighs in his chest, and he finds no salvation in his desperation. Not even when Phainon cards his fingers through his hair, scratching at his scalp as he softly moans into the kiss.

"I'm fine," Mydei says as he pulls away. "I needed to clear my head."

"And did you?" Phainon says a touch out of breath, hair a slight mess as it splays against the wall behind him. If he believes his words, he does not know, but he is thankful he pressures for no detailed answers.

"Yeah," he sighs, though he remains tense. He brings himself to Phainon's neck, and smells nothing amiss when he inhales. It is still the same soft scent of floral shampoos and soap lingering in his hair and skin, nothing like the strange Phainon from before.

"I'm quite glad," Phainon hums, resting the side of his head against Mydei's.

They hold one another, and the dread clinging to his bones lifts bit by bit. Phainon's hand drifts up and down his back, nails tracing the length of his spine, palm rubbing at stiff muscles, fingers kneading, and he melts into him when he rubs against his weak spot. One day, he will tell him about it; share his deepest held secret. But for now, he will appreciate the gentle embrace, feel the warmth engulfing him as ice retreats from his veins.

Phainon must know something is amiss, but he doesn't comment on it. He reclines against the wall, keeping him in his hold for as long as he needs, and allows for Mydei's thoughts to simmer and calm from their maelstrom.

"I didn't realize the crown prince became such an exhibitionist in the short while he was gone," he says after a while and Mydei fully relaxed. "Have I been too polite with keeping a cordial distance in public?"

Mydei instantly prickles and rips himself away. A few people from distant rooftops stare, even some on the streets below have their gazes fixed upon them, and whispers are shared. Embarrassment sears all the way to his ears. With a huff, he pushes off Phainon and crosses his arms.

And he hears Phainon laugh and feels him tug on the cape fixed to his pauldron, telling him he must cleanse himself in the baths in a cheerful intonation. Mydei spares him a glance from his profile, any indignation lost when he beholds his cheer.

Phainon is the dawn, the sun that will always rise and shine down upon the world he will bear. If three years is all he has, he will cherish every moment. Phainon will know of his love and support, be his steadfast companion in this life and the next. He will always push him towards what is right.

Mydei promises this to himself as he takes Phainon's hand in his, threads their fingers together, and allows himself to be pulled along by his ever-bright sun.
